title: TLS Certificate Expiry Watch for Self-Hosted Services
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`), uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=uptime:probe
| stats latest(tls_days_left) as days_left, latest(status) as status by service
| where days_left>=0 AND days_left<21
| sort days_left
description: Lists self-hosted services whose TLS certificates are close to expiry before browser warnings, webhooks, and mobile apps start breaking.
value: Certificate expiry is a classic homelab own goal; a short runway report is much nicer than discovering it from a dead dashboard.
implementation: Forward probe results with remaining TLS lifetime; alert inside your preferred renewal window and verify that automation is truly working.
visualization: Table of services by remaining TLS days.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks which self-hosted websites are getting close to their certificate expiring and causing annoying warnings or outages.
